These checks activate native installation outside postinstall and outside webcontainer; the guarded behavior installs binaries without detecting analysis tools.
The checks separate native installation from postinstall shim rebuilding and skip native placement in webcontainer, fitting portability.
The non-postinstall arm calls the locally defined setup, and its webcontainer return controls s5; s7 calls placeBinary at s8, which contains the rename sink s6.
All placeBinary callers are inside setup after the webcontainer return, and setup has only the non-postinstall caller. Neither function is exported or registered as a callback.
fs is imported from node:fs, and placeBinary links or copies the binary to a temporary file before renaming it to the destination.

Postinstall calls relinkNpmWindowsShims, whose disjunctive early return requires Windows and a present npm executable with lowercased basename npm-cli.js to continue. The presence check is part of the executable test, giving three conjuncts.
The lifecycle, platform and npm-executable checks enable reaching the shim-rebuilding process spawn.
The checks activate npm shim rebuilding on Windows during postinstall with the npm CLI, without testing for analysis instrumentation.
The guarded process runs the npm CLI with rebuild and --ignore-scripts for the wrapper package on Windows, fitting portability.
The postinstall arm calls the locally defined relinkNpmWindowsShims, whose early return controls s12; the spawn sink sits directly in that region.

The sole caller of relinkNpmWindowsShims is the postinstall arm, and its platform/executable early return precedes the only spawnSync call. The function is neither exported nor registered as a callback.
The null check protects the basename test of the same npm_execpath value within one early-return condition, so it belongs to the recorded executable test rather than an additional gate.

Both platform arms install the same native binary; Windows adds executable-suffixed destinations and rewrites the bin map, while the other arm supplies a file mode. This is storage and startup plumbing.
The Windows branch changes executable suffixes and the bin map, while both branches place the same native binary. This check chooses storage and startup plumbing.
